question.text: Which of the following credit rating symbols indicates the highest degree of safety for a long-term debt instrument?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series II-A workbook (page 37), AAA indicates the highest degree of safety for long-term debt instruments and carries the lowest credit risk. The Trap: Option B (A1+) is a short-term rating symbol defined separately on page 38, not a long-term rating. Page 38 also clarifies that plus/minus modifiers apply only to ratings from AA to C, so AA+ is one notch below AAA. Note: Credit ratings are assigned by SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agencies. Keep the long-term scale (AAA to D) separate from the short-term scale (A1 onwards).
